items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name's Dick Allen. What's yours?

ctx.x: What's the number here? 418 North Prayer.
418 North Prayer. My name's Dick Allen. What's yours?
And then Bill Russell is here and over in the corner, Ralph Allen. Okay, good. You might tell where you were born, Mr. Williams.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Yeah, like I'd say, come on Dick, you come play, you want a job, this fella and that fella, yeah.

ctx.x: It must have been the Eagle or something.
Oh, they didn't go by that name, I imagine not, because we mixed up fellas, you know. Yeah. Yeah, like I'd say, come on Dick, you come play, you want a job, this fella and that fella, yeah. Oh yeah.

Pajot played out there too. Mm-hmm. He had a band out there. But not with Henry Martin, a different time? No, I don't think, I don't think. No. No. Because that was before Pajot's time, you know, see, I imagine. Oh yeah. What about Buddy Petit? Did you remember who played with him much?
